newsitem.title: GERMANY: WCM denies interest in Karstadt.
newsitem.headline: WCM denies interest in Karstadt.

text.p: Germany's WCM Beteiligungs und Grundbesitz AG said on Thursday that it still had no interest in buying a stake in German retailer Karstadt AG.
A WCM management board member, Guenter Vollman, told Reuters that market rumours were unfounded.
"There's nothing to the talk of us taking a stake in Karstadt," Vollman said. "The shares are so expensive that WCM does not have any more interest. There are no discussions at the moment."
WCM had said in mid-June that it was no longer interested in buying a 25 percent stake in Karstadt.
WCM majority shareholder Karl Ehlerding told the Handelsblatt daily newspaper on June 18 that "we have put acquiring a stake in Karstadt behind us".
WCM had expressed an interest in buying stakes of 10 percent each in Karstadt held by Deutsche Bank AG and Commerzbank AG but pulled out after finding the banks' asking price too high.
Karstadt shares have been rising this week on speculation that WCM may express new interest in the Essen-based retailer.
Karstadt shares were up 31 marks at 694 marks.
Dutch supermarket group Ahold NV said earlier on Thursday it had no immediate ambitions in the German market in response to market rumours it would buy a stake in Karstadt.
